newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil propelled higher by futures, premiums.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil propelled higher by futures, premiums.

text.p: The tone for NWE gas oil was bullish on Friday as stronger IPE futures combined with firmer premiums to push outright prices up to $5 a tonne higher.
March IPE gas oil closed $4.25 higher at $169 a tonne, helped up on strong U.S heating oil buying.

The bullish tone set by the futures was added to by several other factors. Arbitrage movements to Asia are drawing nearly 300,000 tonnes of physical gas oil eastwards, refinery run cuts in ARA highlight the prospect of increased demand for material from refiners, and domestic Russian agricultural buying interest is expected to grow.
Heating oil barge premiums rose about 75 cents with first half March barges trading at March IPE +75 cents fob ARA and second half March going at March IPE +$1.
Traders said there was a distinct move to buy in March and sell in stronger April.
Diesel barges were broadly stable at about March IPE +$13 fob, having experienced a push upwards yesterday.
Russian gas oil cargoes were not well offered.
"I can only see one and that is not being offered," said one trader.
Premiums were assessed almost $1 stronger at March IPE +$1 cif NWE.
FOD cargo premiums were also about $1 firmer at March IPE +$1-2 cif NWE while EN590 cargo premiums were steady around March IPE +$12-13 cif NWE.
